title: The Lesson #001 — The Down Payment
premise: A young woman is about to put her entire $9,000 tax refund down on a car she can't afford. Boyce is the man waiting two seats over.
lesson: A down payment doesn't make a car affordable. It just makes the first month feel affordable.

shots.camera: tight handheld over-the-shoulder, dealership finance office
shots.action: A woman in her late twenties slides a cashier's check across a desk to a smiling car salesman. She is grinning, proud, certain

dialogue.speaker: WOMAN
dialogue.line: All nine thousand. Put it all down.

shots.notes: Opens mid-scene. The person who is wrong speaks first. Number on screen by second 3.

shots.action: The salesman's pen circles a monthly payment figure on a printed finance sheet: $684 a month for 84 months
The salesman leans back, relaxed and warm, gesturing at the paperwork as if he is doing her a favor

dialogue.speaker: SALESMAN
dialogue.line: With that much down? You basically already own it.

shots.action: The woman glances at the car through the office glass, already picturing herself in it, and reaches for the pen

shots.camera: rack focus from her hand to a man seated two chairs behind, waiting
shots.action: A composed older man in a navy suit sits in the waiting chairs behind her, a folder on his knee. He has been listening the whole time. He does not get up

dialogue.speaker: BOYCE
dialogue.line: Ask him what the car costs. Not the payment. The car.

shots.notes: His arrival is the payoff. He never stands, never raises his voice. One sentence.

shots.action: The salesman's smile holds for a beat too long, then falters. He looks down at the paperwork

shots.camera: insert, the finance sheet, camera slowly tilting down the column
shots.action: The total-of-payments line on the finance sheet comes into focus at the bottom of the page
The woman's expression changes as she reads the number. She sets the pen down without signing
The man in the navy suit turns a page in his own folder, unbothered, having said all he intends to say in the room

dialogue.speaker: BOYCE
dialogue.line: Nine thousand didn't buy you a car. It bought him a customer.

shots.action: The woman walks out of the dealership past the car, car keys not in her hand, phone to her ear

shots.camera: medium close-up, eye level, locked off, shallow depth of field
shots.action: He speaks directly to camera, calm and direct, no gestures, warm but serious

dialogue.speaker: BOYCE
dialogue.line: A down payment doesn't make a car affordable. It makes the first month feel affordable. The dealer doesn't sell you a car, he sells you a payment, and the payment is where he makes his money. Before you sign anything, find the total. If the total scares you, the car was never yours.
